doc.brief: Allows objects to extend and customize deserialization from ui files.
doc.md:
Allows objects to extend and customize deserialization from ui files.

The `GtkBuildable` interface includes methods for setting names and
properties of objects, parsing custom tags and constructing child objects.

It is implemented by all widgets and many of the non-widget objects that are
provided by GTK. The main user of this interface is [`Builder`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Builder).
There should be very little need for applications to call any of these
functions directly.

An object only needs to implement this interface if it needs to extend the
`GtkBuilder` XML format or run any extra routines at deserialization time.

get_buildable_id.brief: Gets the ID of the `buildable` object.
get_buildable_id.md:
Gets the ID of the `buildable` object.

`GtkBuilder` sets the name based on the ID attribute
of the `<object>` tag used to construct the `buildable`.

add_child.md:
Adds a child to `buildable`. `type` is an optional string
describing how the child should be added.

construct_child.brief: Constructs a child of a buildable that has been specified as “constructor” in the UI definition.
construct_child.md:
Constructs a child of a buildable that has been
 specified as “constructor” in the UI definition. This can be used to
 reference a widget created in a `<ui>` tag which is outside
 of the normal GtkBuilder UI definition hierarchy.  A reference to the
 constructed object is returned and becomes owned by the caller.

custom_finished.brief: Similar to gtk_buildable_parser_finished() but is called once for each custom tag handled by the `buildable`.
custom_finished.md:
Similar to gtk_buildable_parser_finished() but is
called once for each custom tag handled by the `buildable`.

custom_tag_end.brief: Called at the end of each custom element handled by the buildable.
custom_tag_end.md:
Called at the end of each custom element handled by
the buildable.

custom_tag_start.brief: Called for each unknown element under `<child>`.
custom_tag_start.md: Called for each unknown element under `<child>`.

get_id.md:
The getter corresponding to `set_id`. Implement this
  if you implement `set_id`.

get_internal_child.brief: Retrieves the internal child called `childname` of the `buildable` object.
get_internal_child.md: Retrieves the internal child called `childname` of the `buildable` object.

parser_finished.brief: Called when a builder finishes the parsing of a UI definition.
parser_finished.md:
Called when a builder finishes the parsing
 of a UI definition. It is normally not necessary to implement this,
 unless you need to perform special cleanup actions. `GtkWindow` sets
 the `GtkWidget:visible` property here.

set_buildable_property.brief: Sets a property of a buildable object.
set_buildable_property.md:
Sets a property of a buildable object.
 It is normally not necessary to implement this, g_object_set_property()
 is used by default. `GtkWindow` implements this to delay showing itself
 (i.e. setting the [`Widget:visible`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:visible) property) until the whole
 interface is created.

set_id.brief: Stores the id attribute given in the `GtkBuilder` UI definition.
set_id.md:
Stores the id attribute given in the `GtkBuilder` UI definition.
  `GtkWidget` stores the name as object data. Implement this method if your
  object has some notion of “ID” and it makes sense to map the XML id
  attribute to it.
